description: NeuraX is a team of six university students combining expertise in AI, software engineering, environmental science, chip design, and mechanical engineering. Our interests span machine learning, computer vision, Earth observation, climate, satellite data, and environmental monitoring. With experience in research and NASA Space Apps, we turn complex challenges into practical solutions by researching deeply, prototyping quickly, and learning together. We value curiosity, collaboration, and impact
summary: AgroTwin is a bilingual crop-rotation decision-support prototype for the Field Shift challenge. It helps farmers and agricultural advisers in Vietnam explore rice-based rotation options using NASA environmental data, local crop references and farmer-declared conditions. NASA POWER supplies regional rainfall, temperature and humidity history; the dashboard brings climate estimates, uncertainty, source citations and three reference rotations into one workflow. Users can inspect evidence, compare constraints and save a discussion draft. A worked example shows a mungbean option blocked when the user declares poor drainage, with the supporting source visible. AgroTwin makes missing evidence explicit and can decline unsupported questions. Its intended value is clearer, more traceable discussions before changing crops. This research prototype does not establish field-level crop suitability or measured gains in yield, profit or water savings; local agronomic review and field validation remain necessary.
details:
PROBLEM AND USERS

Farmers considering a change in a rice-based rotation must connect climate conditions with soil, water management, crop requirements and their own priorities. AgroTwin supports that discussion for farmers and agricultural advisers, using My Thanh in Vietnam as a research case. The study label and geometry are not an independently surveyed farm boundary.

WHAT WE BUILT

A Vietnamese/English dashboard brings map context, historical climate, monthly estimates, evidence inspection and reference-rotation comparison into one workflow. Farmer and Power User views share the same underlying analysis. Users enter known conditions or mark them unknown, inspect constraints and sources, and save a draft for discussion. The three reference sequences are rice-rice-rice, rice-mungbean-rice and rice-baby corn-rice. They are alternatives to explore, not a validated ranking.

NASA DATA AND METHOD

The selected climate pipeline retains 514 months of NASA POWER data from January 1984 through October 2026 at one study coordinate. It checks units, missing observations and calendar coverage, then aggregates rainfall totals and temperature/relative-humidity means. Six climate tasks cover three variables at one- and three-month horizons. Historical same-month means were retained after more complex candidates failed the promotion gate. Empirical residual ranges communicate uncertainty. These are regional monthly research estimates, not daily weather forecasts or measurements at the farm. SMAP and MODIS supply additional regional soil-moisture and vegetation context; their different spatial and temporal support is preserved.

EVIDENCE AND DECISION WORKFLOW

Seventeen bilingual, analyst-authored evidence cards connect local agricultural publications and NASA documentation to supported questions. BM25 and character TF-IDF retrieval are followed by query-support, policy and source-byte checks. The system returns a cited extractive answer or an insufficient-evidence response. Cards retain source URLs, locators and scope; they are not official standards or expert approval. In the worked example, a user-declared poor-drainage condition conflicts with the cited mungbean protocol, so the option is blocked. This does not establish the actual drainage of My Thanh or prove that another crop is suitable.

TOOLS AND IMPLEMENTATION

The dashboard uses React, TypeScript, Vite and MapLibre. Python/FastAPI services support the climate, retrieval and analysis workflows, with NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn used in the research pipeline. Optional ESP32/Web Serial and H1 ingestion support timestamped sensor context. A physical device is not required, and recorded or bench telemetry is distinct from verified field measurements. The public repository includes source, dependency manifests, run instructions, attribution and retained evaluation reports.

VALIDATION AND LIMITS

A reused 2018-2025 retrospective diagnostic records rainfall MAE of 62.74 mm/month; nominal 80% rainfall intervals achieved 67.71% coverage. These are diagnostics against POWER, not an untouched or independent field test. On a small authored set of 8 supported and 8 unsupported questions, the retrieval gate matched evidence for all 8 supported questions and correctly declined 6 of 8 unsupported questions. Two unsupported questions escaped refusal. Source integrity checks do not guarantee that a passage answers a question or applies to a particular farm.

CREATIVITY, INTENDED IMPACT AND NEXT STEPS

AgroTwin connects environmental context to an inspectable decision: which declared condition conflicts with a rotation, which source supports that check, and what remains unknown? The intended benefit is more informed rotation discussions and clearer follow-up measurements. Yield, profit and water savings have not been measured. Crop scores, ranks and probabilities remain unset; agronomic approval is not claimed. Next steps are to validate local inputs and crop rules with specialists, test usability with farmers, and evaluate decision errors in a small pilot.

SI / AI DISCLOSURE

Codex/ChatGPT assisted with development, debugging, documentation, presentation drafts, diagrams and integration. The team-logo background edit used image generation. The demo production used Qwen3-TTS for synthetic narration. These uses do not constitute agronomic validation. Original creation history, third-party attribution and AI assistance are documented in the public project resources. Farmer judgment and local agricultural expertise remain essential.
